description:
Could You Be the First Woman in Space?

Episode 127 of a daily journey through the universe. 👩‍🚀
We fly with Valentina Tereshkova: a textile worker and amateur skydiver who, on June 16, 1963, aged 26, flew Vostok 6, orbiting Earth 48 times in almost three days, more time in space than all American astronauts until then combined.

segments.text: What if you went from a factory job to flying around the Earth forty-eight times? She did.
Valentina Tereshkova worked in a textile factory, and loved skydiving in her free time.
segments.headline: A factory worker and skydiver

segments.text: Skydiving was important. Vostok pilots had to eject and land by parachute.
segments.headline: Parachute skills

segments.text: She was chosen from more than four hundred applicants to train as a cosmonaut.
On June sixteenth, nineteen sixty-three, she launched aboard Vostok six. She was twenty-six years old.
Her radio call sign was Chaika. Seagull.
segments.headline: Call sign: Seagull

segments.text: She orbited Earth forty-eight times, spending almost three days in space. She kept a logbook, took photos of the horizon, and even felt sick, but she kept going.
That was more time in space than all American astronauts had flown, combined, up to then.
segments.headline: More than all US astronauts

segments.text: It would be nineteen years before another woman went to space. Today, many women have flown to space, lived on the space station, and walked in space. And she opened the door.
segments.headline: Opening the door

segments.text: Next stop: Ring of Fire. Which part surprised you most? Tell me in the comments, and follow for the next stop.
